answers.why: Israel and Judah are communities whose land is filled with guilt and whom God has not forsaken.
Judah is paired with Israel as a community not forsaken by God despite its land's guilt.
The Holy One of Israel is the God against whom the nation's land has sinned.
The God of Israel announces judgment against Babylon, which has oppressed his people.
Israel's slain are the people whom Babylon caused to fall.
Judah is paired with Jerusalem as the kingdom whose inhabitants God cast from his presence.
Judah's princes are officials of the kingdom executed by Babylon's king.
Judah is deported from its land, and the next verse counts the captive Jews.
Judah has gone into exile and dwells among the nations.
Israel's splendor is cast down in the destruction of Zion and its kingdom.
Israel's power is cut off before the enemy amid the destruction of the kingdom.
Israel is swallowed up along with its palaces and strongholds.
